Treating the // INFALLIBLE: marker as a contradiction of sk-code's clippy unwrap denial: the two are compatible, so it is recorded as a missing escape hatch

label: rust-anything's method is a nine-stage pipeline (profile, analyze, bridge, record, port.rs, diff, bench, shadow, gate) with the original as the source of truth; sk-code states the byte-for-byte parity standard but has no ordered stage sequence that produces the evidence.

record generates deterministic edge-case inputs from parameter types plus per-parameter semantic traps (string length and case, signed division, overflow edges, float printing, map and sort order) into cases.jsonl and can also capture the original's own test suite with --from-tests; sk-code requires golden fixtures but never says what inputs the recording must contain.

diff reports where the first difference is (return, throw or call N, the JSON path, the kind of difference, and for text the character with context) and groups distinct differences under a stable id so 40 failing cases from one bug read as one line, with --redact printing shapes only; sk-code has no mismatch-reporting rule.

gate is a composite pass/fail over fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, unsafe audit, nothing unported, a recorded failing case for every error path, no unwrap/expect/panic! where the original returns an error unless marked // INFALLIBLE: <why>, build, API, behavior, recording freshness, a 3x-plus-50 line size budget and the cheat guard; sk-code covers fmt/clippy/tests and denies unwrap_used/expect_used/panic via clippy but has zero hits for INFALLIBLE and no size budget.

The cheat guard is three named checks that stop a port passing without porting: literals (three or more 8+ char strings or 5+ significant digit numbers equal to a recorded value the original never spells out, with // recorded-literal: <reason> as the escape), tests (fewer #[test] functions, assertions or more #[ignore]s than at the last passing gate), and recording (a recorded line edited or removed); sk-code has zero hits for cheat, recorded-literal or known-diffs, and this is the highest-value gap for an agent-driven port.

shadow runs both implementations in production, returns the original's result, never lets a Rust error reach a caller, and is selected by RUST_ANYTHING_MODE=old|shadow|new; sk-code has zero hits for shadow, so the staged-rollout method is entirely absent.

bench is deliberately outside gate because speed decides shipping but is not correctness ('every x18n core port was correct and slower'); sk-code mentions benchmarks only as build hygiene (cargo test --benches) and as a precondition for Rayon, so it lacks the rule that a port must be timed against the original before it ships.

A stale recording fails the gate: record saves a fingerprint of the unit's files in recorded-from.json, and when the original changes diff reports a stale recording and exits non-zero while gate fails until re-recorded; sk-code has zero hits for stale or fingerprint, so an upstream change can pass silently.

Corrections the user makes during a port are committed as port rules in rust/RULES.md, one bullet each, added with rules --add and injected into every prompt the tool writes so every later unit and agent keeps them; sk-code has zero hits for RULES.md, so it has no durable-correction mechanism.

'Keep the original's shape' is an explicit port rule: a port keeps the original's units, names and public API (one crate per unit, the same exported functions and classes, the same arguments and errors), the front door keeps the original's commands and flags, and design changes wait until after the port matches; sk-code's naming reference never mentions the original.

A recorded pitfall shows a broken port passing because its case was never recorded (recording silently drops a case whose result JSON cannot hold), and the remedy is to check cases.jsonl holds the inputs and to break the port once to see diff fail; sk-code has no 'prove the check can fail' rule.

A recorded pitfall shows a CLI's recorded writes being invisible because the fixture already held them, with the remedy to record from a fixture whose generated files are stale and to check the *.out folders are not empty; sk-code has no fixture-staleness rule, and this is the finding that speaks most directly to a CLI-shaped app.
